limits: Development evidence from one local Chromium build, one loopback userspace relay, one generated scene algorithm, and one capacity schedule.
Eight generated-seed clusters are not eight independent content families or physical network sources.
Sampled RGB PSNR and a 150 ms pixel-readback deadline are proxies, not human QoE.
Relay cost uses validated feasible clock bounds; possible events include boundary-ambiguous offers.
No pooling with V3, V4, V5, archived native sessions, recorded-video evidence, or simulator/synthetic-controller evidence.
No controller was fitted or promoted by this probe.

prior_turn_v2_checker_abort_reference.failure_class: selected local peer-reflexive classification rejected after TURN-backed ICE connection

prior_turn_v3_failed_capture_reference.failure_class: phase-snapshot guard read an unrecorded remote_candidate_type field after the registered session schedule

prior_turn_v4_gate_failure_reference.failure_class: three sessions missed held-out clock coverage; eight sessions violated V4's registered zero-overflow queue rule

prior_turn_v5_gate_failure_reference.failure_class: two sessions missed held-out coverage at the initial high-phase marker m0002

prior_turn_v6_gate_failure_reference.failure_class: 21 sessions missed final held-out marker m0011 and two also missed m0003

runtime.network_policy: TURN control TCP and relay/queue UDP are loopback-only

transport.candidate_gathering_acceptance: Both peers complete gathering with relay-only candidates and relayProtocol=tcp; candidate errors are zero.
transport.media_acceptance: Each phase must show more than 10 encoded and decoded frames and a finite mean encode time; every phase snapshot must retain the loopback remote address and relay candidate type.
transport.queue_acceptance: Each direction must forward at least 100 packets from the matching TURN allocation source port, with no unexpected sources or send errors. Event replay must exactly match offered, dropped, served, and forwarded packet and wire-byte totals in the ledger. Queue overflow drops are registered delivery outcomes. The capacity integral must be valid and byte conservation error no greater than 1e-6 bytes.
transport.selected_pair_acceptance: Both pairs are nominated and succeeded, use a remote TURN relay candidate, and expose local loopback with relayProtocol=tcp; the local candidate may be relay or peer-reflexive because the registered queue rewrites the remote relay endpoint.
